text:
Mateo Alvarez: seeing failures in the int8 rollout test in staging. A100 is fine, but L4 + some T4 nodes are throwing kernel selection errors. anyone else looking?

Hiro Tanaka: yeah, got a ping from perf suite. looks like the runtime is trying to pick the int8 GEMM kernel path even when the profile was built for sm80 only.

Grace Kim: do we have logs? if it’s the int8 weight-only kernel, it’s usually limited to specific SMs (and sometimes requires `mma` shape support).

Mateo Alvarez: from one of the L4 workers:
```
E1106 09:14:22.913 runtime/kernels.cc:221] quant kernel resolve failed
  model=llama-3-8b
  profile_id=qpl:llama-3-8b:int8:2024-11-05
  gpu="NVIDIA L4" sm=89
  requested_path=int8_weight_only
  error="no compatible kernel found (expected sm80, got sm89)"
W1106 09:14:22.913 runtime/execute.cc:88] falling back to baseline failed: fallback disabled by feature flag
```

Yuki Sato: oof, so we’re not even hitting baseline. why is fallback disabled in staging tests?

Mateo Alvarez: the test harness has `quantization.require_profile=true` to catch misconfigs. it’s doing its job, but we need profile scoping.

Hiro Tanaka: root cause is probably in the compatibility predicate. we check dtype + group size + seq regime, but the GPU arch constraint isn’t being applied early enough (or at all) when resolving the candidate kernel list.

Grace Kim: for L4 (sm89), our int8 path differs. sm80 uses the cutlass int8 kernels we packaged; sm89 wants the newer kernels (or we force fp16/bf16). also T4 is sm75, which definitely won’t work for that int8 weight-only kernel.

Noah Patel: the current resolver does:
1) pick “quantized execution mode” from profile
2) pick kernel family by model arch
3) only then checks GPU capabilities
If step 1 picks int8-only, we’re already in the wrong branch.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. scheduling layer also caches the resolved “execution plan” per (model, profile_id) today. it doesn’t include gpu arch in cache key. so even if one worker resolves on A100 first, others might reuse.

Mateo Alvarez: ah that explains why it’s flaky depending on which worker warms the cache.

Hiro Tanaka: exactly. we need cache key = (model, profile_id, sm, maybe driver/runtime build). otherwise cross-SKU contamination.

Marcus Reed: perf suite runs a mixed matrix (A100 + L4) in the same region, so it’s the perfect storm.

Mina Haddad: jumping in — routing policy is set to canary 10% for quantized path, but runtime still should be safe. from platform side we assumed runtime would “self-fallback” on incompat.

Mateo Alvarez: agreed. staging test has fallback disabled; prod policy won’t. but we still need correctness. propose:
- enforce `hardware_scope` from profile manifest (allowed_sm list)
- include sm in resolver cache key
- when profile incompatible: return “incompatible” reason + increment metric, then fall back to baseline if allowed

Grace Kim: also check kernel constraints: group_size=128 int8 weight-only kernel currently only built for sm80. if we want L4 support, we either compile sm89 variant or publish a separate profile variant.

Hiro Tanaka: I’d rather ship conservative: mark the existing profile as `hardware_scope=[sm80]` and let L4/T4 use fp16 baseline. later we can add `int8_sm89` profile.

Yuki Sato: how do we represent this in the library schema? something like:
- `hardware.gpu_arch: ["sm80"]`
- `runtime.kernel_id: "cutlass_int8_wo_sm80_v3"`
then resolver filters candidates by sm.

Noah Patel: yep. and if someone force-enables quant on an L4-only route, policy engine should still allow fallback to baseline (unless explicitly require).

Mateo Alvarez: action items:
1) fix cache key to include `sm` (Sofia/Noah?)
2) add early compatibility check on profile -> if sm not allowed, return INCOMPATIBLE before selecting kernel path (Hiro/Grace?)
3) update staging harness to keep `require_profile=true` but also surface clearer error message + link to docs

Sofia Ivanova: I can take cache key. we’ll need to invalidate existing cache entries; should be fine.

Hiro Tanaka: I’ll patch the resolver logic + add a unit test that warms on A100 and then resolves on L4 and must not reuse.

Grace Kim: I’ll sanity check the kernel list and confirm which kernels are built for sm89 in our current container. pretty sure none for int8 wo.

deploy-bot: buildkite #runtime-main failed (staging-int8-rollout)
Step: run_quant_rollout_matrix
Error: "no compatible kernel found (expected sm80, got sm89)" (see logs)

Marcus Reed: can we also emit a metric tag for `quant_incompat_reason=sm_mismatch`? would help perf suite triage.

Mateo Alvarez: yes, adding to telemetry. Mina, FYI this is likely the issue behind the earlier “L4 only” failures.

Mina Haddad: yep, thanks. once runtime fixes are in, I’ll re-run the route canary with mixed SKU pool.

Noah Patel: small note: include `compute_capability` not GPU name. naming is messy ("NVIDIA L4" vs "L4"). sm is best.

Hiro Tanaka: makes sense. also, do we want to fail closed or open when profile missing hardware_scope? I vote fail open but log warning (for old profiles).

Mateo Alvarez: fail open for backward compat, but we should require scope for new publish. will loop in Applied ML.

Sofia Ivanova: cache key change PR by EOD. will add a guard so we don’t store “quantized-only plan” unless it’s compatible with the local sm.

Grace Kim: ok. if we ever add sm89 int8, we should keep it separate kernel_id. mixing is risky.

Mateo Alvarez: agreed. thanks all. I’ll post a short summary in #eng-ml so they can update the manifest for the int8 profile to sm80-only for now.
